column3: NKJV has “by the other side of the Jordan,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “and beyond the Jordan.”
NKJV names “God” as the subject, following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “He made them.”
NKJV has “rebuked those who brought them,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “rebuked them.”
NKJV puts “Do not commit adultery” before “Do not murder,” following the order of the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Do not murder” first.
NKJV includes “take up the cross,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “come, follow Me.”
NKJV includes “for those who trust in riches,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God.”
NKJV includes “or wife” and has “father or mother,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks “wife” and has “mother or father.”
